title: Huntik: Secrets & Seekers
summary: Huntik: Secrets & Seekers is an Italian-based animated series that was created and directed by Iginio Straffi. It was animated by Rainbow S.p.A., a studio co-owned by Straffi and Viacom. Both seasons were co-produced by Rai Fiction and the first was co-produced by Big Bocca Productions. The visual designs, artwork, music, and story writing were all done at Rainbow in Italy while some scriptwriting and voicing were done in the United States. The series is an action-adventure comedy that follows the team of Lok Lambert, Sophie Casterwill, Zhalia Moon, and mentor Dante Vale around the globe in search of ancient Amulets that can summon powerful beings known as Titans in order to battle the forces of evil. The show features a variety of real-world historical locations, and one of Straffi's goals for the show was to give viewers "the opportunity to learn about Italian and European culture."

sections.heading: Production
sections.wikitext:
The basic premise of the show was already laid out and publicized in October 2006, with the first season having a budget of approximately 8.62 million US dollars.https://kidscreen.com/2006/10/01/cool-20061001/ The titular word "Huntik" comes from a mix of the words "antique", to mean something "old, legendary and mysterious" and "hunting" [for treasures].https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AjYWmvnOqQo The second season was an investment of 10 million US dollars.https://kidscreen.com/2011/03/25/rainbows-huntik-gets-second-season/ After creator [[Iginio Straffi]] drew the initial concepts of ''Huntik'', [[Sean Molyneaux]], writer and story-supervisor of fellow-Straffi creation ''Winx Club'', met with Straffi and Upper Deck producers to polish some details of the show's premise in the animation studio Rainbow S.p.A. Molyneaux, who was already familiar with Upper Deck personnel from his work on ''Yugi-Oh'', was also specifically tasked with creating the "Show Bible", a "master document that covers the entire program: all the characters, all the development that will take place, all of the backstories, episode synopses and the plot–past, present and future." The first season involved around three years of production,https://huntik-france.weebly.com/artbook while the second one took almost a year and a half.https://web.archive.org/web/20201214030740/http://www.iginiostraffi.com/wp-content/uploads/2009/10/vanity-fair-laggi%C3%B9-dove-pettinano-le-bambole-14-10-2008.pdf
''The production of Huntik was a considerable and exciting project, involving hundreds of professionals working for three full years, bringing together the best talent in the field of animation. The results truly seem to me to be worthy of the effort, but ultimately, that will be for you to judge.'' [translated from Italian by original source]
- Iginio Straffi
''Huntik: Secrets & Seeker''s' production efforts were split across many different locations. The writing was done in the United States, while the computer graphics, backgrounds, design and art was all done in Italy, and the "nuts and bolts animation" was done in Korea. The original voice acting was done in English at NYAV Post studio, and dubbed using that as a guide into other languages. However, the music, sound effects, as well as the episode and art direction, were all also done in Italy, as were the supervision of the scripts, namely by Maurizio De Angelis. As such, writers and artists had to communicate via e-mail. Designers would start off with descriptions from the script or the show Bible itself; and from then, they would either write back to Molyneaux for more details or "go off in their own direction".
''I try to keep my descriptions minimalist at first, maybe mentioning a single important fact (maybe a personality trait, or a physical trait in the case of a [[Titans|Titan]]), hoping that maybe this will inspire the designer.''
- Sean Molyneauxhttps://web.archive.org/web/20120723191939/http://blog.dvdplanet.com/2009/09/an-interview-with-the-folks-behind-huntik/
Creative director [[Simone Borselli]] stated that it took a year to understand what they wanted art-wise, and another year to define the characters, "from their clothes to their attitude". Borselli added that he even had to "anticipate fashion trends", as the show would only come out at least two years later. Some of the main characters' designs were inspired by actors: [[Dante Vale]] by Johnny Depp, [[Zhalia Moon]] by Demi Moore and [[Sophie Casterwill]] by Gwyneth Paltrow. To illustrate the backgrounds of the series, the artists studied photos and visual maps online. Tommaso Gomez, background supervisor, explained that the large number of backgrounds were a challenge, and he had to think of some of them as a "movie set".
''In particular, [[the Professor's castle]] took a lot of work, because it spans two episodes and big fight takes place there. For this, all the locations in the castle were perfectly connected like a movie set.'' ''One of the most important things is that I really lived in many of the cities... and places where the Huntik series is located. Especially Venice, [[Prague]], and Paris where I lived for a long time. This helped me reproduce the right feelings of the locations in the cartoon... according to what I directly felt living in these cities.'' [translated from Italian by original source; slightly adapted]
- Tommaso Gomez
The issue of violence being emulated by children was overcome by the use of [[Titans]] and other [[magic]] as fighting tools.
''In Huntik, the issue of violence, which could be emulated by children, is overcome by having monsters fight instead of humans. And, if the men are involved, the punch in the face is replaced with an "energy ball," which is decidedly difficult to replicate at home.'' [translated from Italian]
- Simone Borselli
Borselli reviewed all 11700 scenes of the first season three times to check on the animation, and another two times per scene for the audio effects.

sections.heading: Broadcasting
sections.wikitext:
The [[Season 1|first season]] was initially announced [http://kidscreen.com/2006/10/01/cool-20061001/ here] in 2006 for a broadcast date of early 2008, but it was delayed by a year. It eventually premiered on The CW's CW4Kids block in the United States and on Jetix in the UK, both beginning on 3 January 2009. Following weeks of previews, it premiered in Italy on Rai Due on 12 January 2009. The first season ended in the UK on 29 January, in Italy on 16 February, and in the US on 5 September.

A tie-in [[Huntik Trading Card Game]] was released beginning on February 17, 2009, with [[TCG:Secrets and Seekers|Secrets and Seekers]] and concluding with the October 09, 2009, release of [[Omens and Legacies]].

The American company Viacom became a co-owner of Rainbow S.p.A. ahead of the [[Season 2|second season's]] premiere in 2011. Both seasons of ''Huntik'' began to be broadcast on Viacom's Nickelodeon channels worldwide. The [[Season 2|second season]] premiered on September 17, 2011, on Rai 2 in Italy, on April 16, 2012, on CITV in the UK, and April 21, 2013, on Nicktoons in the US. The final episode aired in Italy on December 11, 2011, in the UK on May 30, 2012, and in the US on October 15, 2015, with episodes 38 through 52 only airing on Netflix.

sections.heading: Premise
sections.wikitext:
''Huntik Secrets and Seekers [[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sic sic]] is a cartoon that aims to be a cultured alternative to the trend of Japanese manga or American cartoons, giving our children the opportunity to learn about Italian and European culture while having fun.'' [translated from Italian]
- Iginio Straffihttps://www.e-duesse.it/giocattoli/huntik-12-di-share-per-raidue/
Long before our time, humanity fought against an evil of unimaginable power. The darkness was broken only by the Seekers, humans able to invoke legendary creatures, the [[Titans]], into their own plane of existence. With the Titans executing their every order, the first Seekers fought against the dark forces of the underworld and against themselves. Centuries went by, and one by one, the Titans were hidden; some were buried following grueling battles, while others were merely forgotten as time passed. The magical and powerful creatures lie hidden and dormant in the most remote parts of the universe, waiting to be awoken by a new group of Seekers. After centuries passed, the Seekers divided themselves into groups in order to find traces and clues of past and extinct populations in order to reveal the mystery of the Titans. One such division, the [[Huntik Foundation]], travels in search of these answers - from the tip of South America to Europe; from North America to the African terrains. Only the most worthy of Seekers are able to invoke the Titans and benefit from their unbelievable powers. But there are those who plot in the shadows: the secretive [[The Organization|Organization]], led by [[the Professor]], is another division of Seekers and wants to possess the Titans' powers for their own evil plans.

sections.heading: Reception
sections.wikitext:
Writing for Common Sense Media, Will Wade praised the show's animation, action sequences, story and the [[Titans]]' designs. However, he reveals negative opinions when some parts are looked at closer, highlighting the implausibility of certain aspects that is ultimately overlooked by most of the young target audience. Wade gave an overall score of 3 out of 5 stars for ''Huntik: Secrets & Seekers''.https://www.commonsensemedia.org/tv-reviews/huntik Reviewing just the first five episodes contained on the first [[DVDs|DVD]] of the Australian/New Zealand release, Mark Beresford of Impulse Gamer stated that "some of the music and animation shows sign of a non established franchise budget. [However,] the five episodes released on this disk are pretty addictive and will leave you wanting to get your hands on the rest of the series." The website's ultimate numerical review was of 6.5 out of 10.https://www.impulsegamer.com/dvdhuntiksecretsandseeker.html More than 17 years after the original broadcast of ''Huntik'', Sterling Ulrich of CBR claimed the show was a "perfect 2-Season gem", highlighting its original European aestehtic that seperates it from American and Japanese shows of the same genre, but critizing some of the animation.
''Huntik's animation was somewhat hit-or-miss; while certain scenes looked great, others were clearly victims of a limited budget. That problem only grew worse in the second season, which replaced much of the hand-drawn animation with cheaper Flash animation. Despite that,'' ''Huntik's character and monster designs were always a highlight. Music was one of the series' strengths as well. The intro theme, "[[Huntik Go]]," was a memorable rock piece that built up excitement for every episode.'' [...] ''Even if it remains at just two seasons, Huntik is a solid series that deserves more recognition.''
- Sterling Ulrich, CBRhttps://www.cbr.com/nickelodeon-huntik-secrets-seekers-fantasy-perfect-seasons/
sections.text:
Writing for Common Sense Media, Will Wade praised the show's animation, action sequences, story and the Titans' designs. However, he reveals negative opinions when some parts are looked at closer, highlighting the implausibility of certain aspects that is ultimately overlooked by most of the young target audience. Wade gave an overall score of 3 out of 5 stars for Huntik: Secrets & Seekers.

Reviewing just the first five episodes contained on the first DVD of the Australian/New Zealand release, Mark Beresford of Impulse Gamer stated that "some of the music and animation shows sign of a non established franchise budget. [However,] the five episodes released on this disk are pretty addictive and will leave you wanting to get your hands on the rest of the series." The website's ultimate numerical review was of 6.5 out of 10.

More than 17 years after the original broadcast of Huntik, Sterling Ulrich of CBR claimed the show was a "perfect 2-Season gem", highlighting its original European aestehtic that seperates it from American and Japanese shows of the same genre, but critizing some of the animation. Huntik's animation was somewhat hit-or-miss; while certain scenes looked great, others were clearly victims of a limited budget. That problem only grew worse in the second season, which replaced much of the hand-drawn animation with cheaper Flash animation. Despite that, Huntik's character and monster designs were always a highlight. Music was one of the series' strengths as well. The intro theme, "Huntik Go," was a memorable rock piece that built up excitement for every episode. [...] Even if it remains at just two seasons, Huntik is a solid series that deserves more recognition. 
 - Sterling Ulrich, CBR

sections.heading: Season 1
sections.wikitext:
[[File:S1 Dante poster.jpg|thumb]]
Lok's father, [[Eathon Lambert]], has been missing for ten years, and the only thing Lok has to remember him by is an ancient jar. When that jar is accidentally broken, Lok discovers a journal that discusses the mysterious Titans. The jar also contained an Amulet, although Lok doesn't know what it is at the time. Now Lok is teaming up with The Huntik Foundation to find and bond with Titans before the Professor, [[DeFoe]], [[Grier]], and the rest of the evil [[The Organization|Organization]] use them to take over the world.

Using [[Eathon Lambert's journal]], the team follows a series of clues in an attempt to find Lok's father. However, the search reveals a mysterious connection between Eathon and the Professor as well as clues to uncover the fabled [[Amulet of Will]], which is necessary for awakening [[Lord Casterwill]]'s [[Legendary Titans]].

sections.heading: Season 2
sections.wikitext:
[[File:S2 Lok Kipperin Willblade poster.jpg|thumb]]
With the defeat of the Professor, a new menace has arrived. Rassimov has become stronger, and a new [[The Organization|Organization]] has formed under [[Wilder]]. Having trained since their last battle with [[the Professor]], [[Lok Lambert]], [[Dante Vale]], [[Sophie Casterwill]], and [[Zhalia Moon]] must now face this new menace. To help with their adventures, a new Seeker, [[Den Fears]], is recruited to face off against the [[Blood Spiral Brotherhood]]. In addition to this new member, the power of [[Powerbonding]] has been unleashed.

Having discovered [[Eathon Lambert|Eathon Lambert's]] Holotome, the [[Huntik Foundation]] begins to investigate the Holotome's riddles concerning the prophecies of the ancient [[Seeker]], [[Nostradamus]]. The truth about the [[Casterwill family]] becomes revealed bit by bit, beginning with the discovery of a legendary sword, the [[Willblade]].

full_text:
Huntik: Secrets & Seekers is an Italian-based animated series that was created and directed by Iginio Straffi. It was animated by Rainbow S.p.A., a studio co-owned by Straffi and Viacom. Both seasons were co-produced by Rai Fiction and the first was co-produced by Big Bocca Productions. The visual designs, artwork, music, and story writing were all done at Rainbow in Italy while some scriptwriting and voicing were done in the United States. The series is an action-adventure comedy that follows the team of Lok Lambert, Sophie Casterwill, Zhalia Moon, and mentor Dante Vale around the globe in search of ancient Amulets that can summon powerful beings known as Titans in order to battle the forces of evil. The show features a variety of real-world historical locations, and one of Straffi's goals for the show was to give viewers "the opportunity to learn about Italian and European culture."

== Production ==
The basic premise of the show was already laid out and publicized in October 2006, with the first season having a budget of approximately 8.62 million US dollars. The titular word "Huntik" comes from a mix of the words "antique", to mean something "old, legendary and mysterious" and "hunting" [for treasures]. The second season was an investment of 10 million US dollars.

After creator Iginio Straffi drew the initial concepts of Huntik, Sean Molyneaux, writer and story-supervisor of fellow-Straffi creation Winx Club, met with Straffi and Upper Deck producers to polish some details of the show's premise in the animation studio Rainbow S.p.A. Molyneaux, who was already familiar with Upper Deck personnel from his work on Yugi-Oh, was also specifically tasked with creating the "Show Bible", a "master document that covers the entire program: all the characters, all the development that will take place, all of the backstories, episode synopses and the plot–past, present and future." while the second one took almost a year and a half.The production of Huntik was a considerable and exciting project, involving hundreds of professionals working for three full years, bringing together the best talent in the field of animation. The results truly seem to me to be worthy of the effort, but ultimately, that will be for you to judge. [translated from Italian by original source]
- Iginio Straffi

Creative director Simone Borselli stated that it took a year to understand what they wanted art-wise, and another year to define the characters, "from their clothes to their attitude". Borselli added that he even had to "anticipate fashion trends", as the show would only come out at least two years later. Some of the main characters' designs were inspired by actors: Dante Vale by Johnny Depp, Zhalia Moon by Demi Moore and Sophie Casterwill by Gwyneth Paltrow. To illustrate the backgrounds of the series, the artists studied photos and visual maps online.Long before our time, humanity fought against an evil of unimaginable power. The darkness was broken only by the Seekers, humans able to invoke legendary creatures, the Titans, into their own plane of existence. With the Titans executing their every order, the first Seekers fought against the dark forces of the underworld and against themselves. Centuries went by, and one by one, the Titans were hidden; some were buried following grueling battles, while others were merely forgotten as time passed. The magical and powerful creatures lie hidden and dormant in the most remote parts of the universe, waiting to be awoken by a new group of Seekers.

After centuries passed, the Seekers divided themselves into groups in order to find traces and clues of past and extinct populations in order to reveal the mystery of the Titans. One such division, the Huntik Foundation, travels in search of these answers - from the tip of South America to Europe; from North America to the African terrains. Only the most worthy of Seekers are able to invoke the Titans and benefit from their unbelievable powers. But there are those who plot in the shadows: the secretive Organization, led by the Professor, is another division of Seekers and wants to possess the Titans' powers for their own evil plans.

== Reception ==
Writing for Common Sense Media, Will Wade praised the show's animation, action sequences, story and the Titans' designs. However, he reveals negative opinions when some parts are looked at closer, highlighting the implausibility of certain aspects that is ultimately overlooked by most of the young target audience. Wade gave an overall score of 3 out of 5 stars for Huntik: Secrets & Seekers.

Reviewing just the first five episodes contained on the first DVD of the Australian/New Zealand release, Mark Beresford of Impulse Gamer stated that "some of the music and animation shows sign of a non established franchise budget. [However,] the five episodes released on this disk are pretty addictive and will leave you wanting to get your hands on the rest of the series." The website's ultimate numerical review was of 6.5 out of 10.

More than 17 years after the original broadcast of Huntik, Sterling Ulrich of CBR claimed the show was a "perfect 2-Season gem", highlighting its original European aestehtic that seperates it from American and Japanese shows of the same genre, but critizing some of the animation. Huntik's animation was somewhat hit-or-miss; while certain scenes looked great, others were clearly victims of a limited budget. That problem only grew worse in the second season, which replaced much of the hand-drawn animation with cheaper Flash animation. Despite that, Huntik's character and monster designs were always a highlight. Music was one of the series' strengths as well. The intro theme, "Huntik Go," was a memorable rock piece that built up excitement for every episode. [...] Even if it remains at just two seasons, Huntik is a solid series that deserves more recognition. 
 - Sterling Ulrich, CBR

==Season 1 ==

Lok's father, Eathon Lambert, has been missing for ten years, and the only thing Lok has to remember him by is an ancient jar. When that jar is accidentally broken, Lok discovers a journal that discusses the mysterious Titans. The jar also contained an Amulet, although Lok doesn't know what it is at the time. Now Lok is teaming up with The Huntik Foundation to find and bond with Titans before the Professor, DeFoe, Grier, and the rest of the evil Organization use them to take over the world.

Using Eathon Lambert's journal, the team follows a series of clues in an attempt to find Lok's father. However, the search reveals a mysterious connection between Eathon and the Professor as well as clues to uncover the fabled Amulet of Will, which is necessary for awakening Lord Casterwill's Legendary Titans.

==Season 2 ==

With the defeat of the Professor, a new menace has arrived. Rassimov has become stronger, and a new Organization has formed under Wilder. Having trained since their last battle with the Professor, Lok Lambert, Dante Vale, Sophie Casterwill, and Zhalia Moon must now face this new menace. To help with their adventures, a new Seeker, Den Fears, is recruited to face off against the Blood Spiral Brotherhood. In addition to this new member, the power of Powerbonding has been unleashed.

Having discovered Eathon Lambert's Holotome, the Huntik Foundation begins to investigate the Holotome's riddles concerning the prophecies of the ancient Seeker, Nostradamus. The truth about the Casterwill family becomes revealed bit by bit, beginning with the discovery of a legendary sword, the Willblade.

Huntik.it |youtube = [https://www.youtube.com/@HuntikOfficial @HuntikOfficial] }} '''''Huntik: Secrets & Seekers''''' is an Italian-based animated series that was created and directed by [[Iginio Straffi]]. It was animated by Rainbow S.p.A., a studio co-owned by Straffi and Viacom. Both seasons were co-produced by Rai Fiction and the first was co-produced by Big Bocca Productions. The visual designs, artwork, music, and story writing were all done at Rainbow in Italy while some scriptwriting and voicing were done in the United States. The series is an action-adventure comedy that follows the team of [[Lok Lambert]], [[Sophie Casterwill]], [[Zhalia Moon]], and mentor [[Dante Vale]] around the globe in search of ancient [[Amulets]] that can summon powerful beings known as [[Titans]] in order to battle the forces of evil. The show features a variety of real-world historical locations, and one of Straffi's goals for the show was to give viewers "the opportunity to learn about Italian and European culture." == Production == The basic premise of the show was already laid out and publicized in October 2006, with the first season having a budget of approximately 8.62 million US dollars.https://kidscreen.com/2006/10/01/cool-20061001/ The titular word "Huntik" comes from a mix of the words "antique", to mean something "old, legendary and mysterious" and "hunting" [for treasures].https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AjYWmvnOqQo The second season was an investment of 10 million US dollars.https://kidscreen.com/2011/03/25/rainbows-huntik-gets-second-season/ After creator [[Iginio Straffi]] drew the initial concepts of ''Huntik'', [[Sean Molyneaux]], writer and story-supervisor of fellow-Straffi creation ''Winx Club'', met with Straffi and Upper Deck producers to polish some details of the show's premise in the animation studio Rainbow S.p.A. Molyneaux, who was already familiar with Upper Deck personnel from his work on ''Yugi-Oh'', was also specifically tasked with creating the "Show Bible", a "master document that covers the entire program: all the characters, all the development that will take place, all of the backstories, episode synopses and the plot–past, present and future." The first season involved around three years of production,https://huntik-france.weebly.com/artbook while the second one took almost a year and a half.https://web.archive.org/web/20201214030740/http://www.iginiostraffi.com/wp-content/uploads/2009/10/vanity-fair-laggi%C3%B9-dove-pettinano-le-bambole-14-10-2008.pdf
''The production of Huntik was a considerable and exciting project, involving hundreds of professionals working for three full years, bringing together the best talent in the field of animation. The results truly seem to me to be worthy of the effort, but ultimately, that will be for you to judge.'' [translated from Italian by original source]
- Iginio Straffi
''Huntik: Secrets & Seeker''s' production efforts were split across many different locations. The writing was done in the United States, while the computer graphics, backgrounds, design and art was all done in Italy, and the "nuts and bolts animation" was done in Korea. The original voice acting was done in English at NYAV Post studio, and dubbed using that as a guide into other languages. However, the music, sound effects, as well as the episode and art direction, were all also done in Italy, as were the supervision of the scripts, namely by Maurizio De Angelis. As such, writers and artists had to communicate via e-mail. Designers would start off with descriptions from the script or the show Bible itself; and from then, they would either write back to Molyneaux for more details or "go off in their own direction".
''I try to keep my descriptions minimalist at first, maybe mentioning a single important fact (maybe a personality trait, or a physical trait in the case of a [[Titans|Titan]]), hoping that maybe this will inspire the designer.''
- Sean Molyneauxhttps://web.archive.org/web/20120723191939/http://blog.dvdplanet.com/2009/09/an-interview-with-the-folks-behind-huntik/
Creative director [[Simone Borselli]] stated that it took a year to understand what they wanted art-wise, and another year to define the characters, "from their clothes to their attitude". Borselli added that he even had to "anticipate fashion trends", as the show would only come out at least two years later. Some of the main characters' designs were inspired by actors: [[Dante Vale]] by Johnny Depp, [[Zhalia Moon]] by Demi Moore and [[Sophie Casterwill]] by Gwyneth Paltrow. To illustrate the backgrounds of the series, the artists studied photos and visual maps online. Tommaso Gomez, background supervisor, explained that the large number of backgrounds were a challenge, and he had to think of some of them as a "movie set".
''In particular, [[the Professor's castle]] took a lot of work, because it spans two episodes and big fight takes place there. For this, all the locations in the castle were perfectly connected like a movie set.'' ''One of the most important things is that I really lived in many of the cities... and places where the Huntik series is located. Especially Venice, [[Prague]], and Paris where I lived for a long time. This helped me reproduce the right feelings of the locations in the cartoon... according to what I directly felt living in these cities.'' [translated from Italian by original source; slightly adapted]
- Tommaso Gomez
The issue of violence being emulated by children was overcome by the use of [[Titans]] and other [[magic]] as fighting tools.
''In Huntik, the issue of violence, which could be emulated by children, is overcome by having monsters fight instead of humans. And, if the men are involved, the punch in the face is replaced with an "energy ball," which is decidedly difficult to replicate at home.'' [translated from Italian]
- Simone Borselli
Borselli reviewed all 11700 scenes of the first season three times to check on the animation, and another two times per scene for the audio effects. ==Broadcasting == The [[Season 1|first season]] was initially announced [http://kidscreen.com/2006/10/01/cool-20061001/ here] in 2006 for a broadcast date of early 2008, but it was delayed by a year. It eventually premiered on The CW's CW4Kids block in the United States and on Jetix in the UK, both beginning on 3 January 2009. Following weeks of previews, it premiered in Italy on Rai Due on 12 January 2009. The first season ended in the UK on 29 January, in Italy on 16 February, and in the US on 5 September. A tie-in [[Huntik Trading Card Game]] was released beginning on February 17, 2009, with [[TCG:Secrets and Seekers|Secrets and Seekers]] and concluding with the October 09, 2009, release of [[Omens and Legacies]]. The American company Viacom became a co-owner of Rainbow S.p.A. ahead of the [[Season 2|second season's]] premiere in 2011. Both seasons of ''Huntik'' began to be broadcast on Viacom's Nickelodeon channels worldwide. The [[Season 2|second season]] premiered on September 17, 2011, on Rai 2 in Italy, on April 16, 2012, on CITV in the UK, and April 21, 2013, on Nicktoons in the US. The final episode aired in Italy on December 11, 2011, in the UK on May 30, 2012, and in the US on October 15, 2015, with episodes 38 through 52 only airing on Netflix. ==Premise==
''Huntik Secrets and Seekers [[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sic sic]] is a cartoon that aims to be a cultured alternative to the trend of Japanese manga or American cartoons, giving our children the opportunity to learn about Italian and European culture while having fun.'' [translated from Italian]
- Iginio Straffihttps://www.e-duesse.it/giocattoli/huntik-12-di-share-per-raidue/
Long before our time, humanity fought against an evil of unimaginable power. The darkness was broken only by the Seekers, humans able to invoke legendary creatures, the [[Titans]], into their own plane of existence. With the Titans executing their every order, the first Seekers fought against the dark forces of the underworld and against themselves. Centuries went by, and one by one, the Titans were hidden; some were buried following grueling battles, while others were merely forgotten as time passed. The magical and powerful creatures lie hidden and dormant in the most remote parts of the universe, waiting to be awoken by a new group of Seekers. After centuries passed, the Seekers divided themselves into groups in order to find traces and clues of past and extinct populations in order to reveal the mystery of the Titans. One such division, the [[Huntik Foundation]], travels in search of these answers - from the tip of South America to Europe; from North America to the African terrains. Only the most worthy of Seekers are able to invoke the Titans and benefit from their unbelievable powers. But there are those who plot in the shadows: the secretive [[The Organization|Organization]], led by [[the Professor]], is another division of Seekers and wants to possess the Titans' powers for their own evil plans. == Reception == Writing for Common Sense Media, Will Wade praised the show's animation, action sequences, story and the [[Titans]]' designs. However, he reveals negative opinions when some parts are looked at closer, highlighting the implausibility of certain aspects that is ultimately overlooked by most of the young target audience. Wade gave an overall score of 3 out of 5 stars for ''Huntik: Secrets & Seekers''.https://www.commonsensemedia.org/tv-reviews/huntik Reviewing just the first five episodes contained on the first [[DVDs|DVD]] of the Australian/New Zealand release, Mark Beresford of Impulse Gamer stated that "some of the music and animation shows sign of a non established franchise budget. [However,] the five episodes released on this disk are pretty addictive and will leave you wanting to get your hands on the rest of the series." The website's ultimate numerical review was of 6.5 out of 10.https://www.impulsegamer.com/dvdhuntiksecretsandseeker.html More than 17 years after the original broadcast of ''Huntik'', Sterling Ulrich of CBR claimed the show was a "perfect 2-Season gem", highlighting its original European aestehtic that seperates it from American and Japanese shows of the same genre, but critizing some of the animation.
''Huntik's animation was somewhat hit-or-miss; while certain scenes looked great, others were clearly victims of a limited budget. That problem only grew worse in the second season, which replaced much of the hand-drawn animation with cheaper Flash animation. Despite that,'' ''Huntik's character and monster designs were always a highlight. Music was one of the series' strengths as well. The intro theme, "[[Huntik Go]]," was a memorable rock piece that built up excitement for every episode.'' [...] ''Even if it remains at just two seasons, Huntik is a solid series that deserves more recognition.''
- Sterling Ulrich, CBRhttps://www.cbr.com/nickelodeon-huntik-secrets-seekers-fantasy-perfect-seasons/
==[[Season 1]] == [[File:S1 Dante poster.jpg|thumb]] Lok's father, [[Eathon Lambert]], has been missing for ten years, and the only thing Lok has to remember him by is an ancient jar. When that jar is accidentally broken, Lok discovers a journal that discusses the mysterious Titans. The jar also contained an Amulet, although Lok doesn't know what it is at the time. Now Lok is teaming up with The Huntik Foundation to find and bond with Titans before the Professor, [[DeFoe]], [[Grier]], and the rest of the evil [[The Organization|Organization]] use them to take over the world. Using [[Eathon Lambert's journal]], the team follows a series of clues in an attempt to find Lok's father. However, the search reveals a mysterious connection between Eathon and the Professor as well as clues to uncover the fabled [[Amulet of Will]], which is necessary for awakening [[Lord Casterwill]]'s [[Legendary Titans]]. ==[[Season 2]] == [[File:S2 Lok Kipperin Willblade poster.jpg|thumb]] With the defeat of the Professor, a new menace has arrived. Rassimov has become stronger, and a new [[The Organization|Organization]] has formed under [[Wilder]]. Having trained since their last battle with [[the Professor]], [[Lok Lambert]], [[Dante Vale]], [[Sophie Casterwill]], and [[Zhalia Moon]] must now face this new menace. To help with their adventures, a new Seeker, [[Den Fears]], is recruited to face off against the [[Blood Spiral Brotherhood]]. In addition to this new member, the power of [[Powerbonding]] has been unleashed. Having discovered [[Eathon Lambert|Eathon Lambert's]] Holotome, the [[Huntik Foundation]] begins to investigate the Holotome's riddles concerning the prophecies of the ancient [[Seeker]], [[Nostradamus]]. The truth about the [[Casterwill family]] becomes revealed bit by bit, beginning with the discovery of a legendary sword, the [[Willblade]]. ==Posters== Huntik Season 1 Full Poster.png|Season 1 Poster Overlos poster.jpg|Season 1 Poster S1 Netflix poster crop.jpeg|Season 1 Netflix Poster S1 Team Poster.png|Season 1 Poster S2 Poster Powerbonded Kipperin Lok.png|Season 2 Poster Huntik Netflix Home Poster.png|Season 2 Poster Caliban Kipperin Lok Netflix Poster.jpg|Season 2 Netflix Poster Huntik Season 2 poster.jpg|Season 2 Poster S2 streaming banner.jpg|Season 2 Netflix Poster ==International Titles== {{International Titles |FR = Huntik, le choc des titans |FR translation = Huntik, clash of the titans}} == References == [[Category:Content]]
